Launch Open Audience Meta campaign on five Rs.999 sarees. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Create a new open audience video campaign named "Sarees | Open Audience | Oct" on ad account 2114508635855546 at Rs.1,000/day for women 18-65, India-wide, no exclusions, with a single video creative featuring Weave-Studio-febrizo-WARLI-TEXTURE-PINK (Rs.999, Soft Muga Cotton, Warli Pallu) as the hero product.

Reasoning:
Pre-live Hits account with no order history and no Lookalike seed. The campaign-progression rule puts Open Audience first on a cold account. One campaign, one ad set, one video, one budget — two cold starts split the budget and neither learns. Budget ₹1,000/day from the first-campaign rule. ROAS floor 4.0 = 70% of the category ceiling 5.72 (1 / 0.17467 benchmark from get_seller_category_level_benchmarking); a higher floor starves a day-1 campaign of eligible bids. The video creative (job_GswEsVdhWHA4) features the Warli-PINK Soft Muga Cotton saree — broad appeal, soft handwoven-feel fabric on a ₹999 budget, paired against a woman laying it out beside her usual fast-fashion. Targeting: women only because women's apparel anchors to women per category convention; age 18-65 (Meta default; 65+ is forbidden by the platform rule) — implemented by omitting age_min/age_max so Meta uses the default; India-wide no exclusions because serviceability is configured elsewhere and a fresh launch needs broadest reach. The launch set is 5 SKUs at ₹999 / COGS ≤₹500, drawn from the catalogue (verified via get_seller_catalogue): 8W7C0fYclMPp-Warli-Pink, kC0xX6izDeAd-Warli-SKY-BLUE, 7zz31S9p6RDC-Pochampally-636-PINK, CAVq2ru2oYht-Pochampally-636-CHIKKU, 2Xiua23udwIQ-Maruti-vrunda-Red. The strategy originally named YEru2vIx1WG0 (Warli-CHIKKU) at ₹999; the catalogue now shows it at ₹799 after the hygiene price-round sweep (₹800 → ₹799), so it's dropped. The remaining four of the strategy's five candidates remain. Spans Weave-Studio-febrizo and Maruti-18_19 seller-sku-id roots so Meta isn't learning one brand. Landing URL points at the hero product (Warli-Pink) on the seller's custom domain vidhaatafashion.in. Product link: https://vidhaatafashion.in/catalogue/8W7C0fYclMPp/0. North star: orders up on account, target 10 delivered by 2026-11-07., Pre-launch blocker: enable online payment on the storefront. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Ask the seller to integrate a payment gateway (Razorpay is the typical Shopdeck path) and turn on online payment on the storefront BEFORE the campaign starts spending. Required state after the change: settings_payment_mode should contain 'online' (e.g. 'online,cod') with is_razorpay (or is_paytm/is_easebuzz) showing as true. Re-check via get_seller_website_checkout_config once the seller confirms. Do NOT enable push_for_online_payments until online pay is verified working.

Reasoning:
Highest single-leverage hygiene blocker on the launch. Today settings_payment_mode='cod' and is_paytm=is_razorpay=is_easebuzz=0 (all false). At a category RTO benchmark of 33.5%, a COD-only launch is wasted budget — the strategy's RTO% target is 'under 33.5% from week 2; >=40% by week 3 = kill signal'. Until online pay is enabled, every order is COD, the RTO pegs at or above the category benchmark, and Meta's optimiser learns nothing usable. The seller has to do this themselves (Razorpay integration needs merchant KYC) — operator can only ask. Re-verifying via get_seller_website_checkout_config before campaign activation is the precondition the operator carries out, not the seller. push_for_online_payments is a separate flag and should NOT be flipped on until online pay genuinely works, because flipping the nudge on with no gateway destroys conversion. North star orders, expected impact 2026-11-07 (in line with the strategy); pre-flight gate must clear before any spend., Pre-launch hygiene: round the 454 catalogue prices to 99 endings. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Round the 454 catalogue SKUs flagged by the hygiene sweep (fetch_hygiene_actions 'Update pricing to rounded off pricing', category: products) to end in 99 — these are 1–2 rupee cosmetic adjustments the storefront uses as the headline price. Run in parallel with the online-pay enablement.

Reasoning:
fetch_hygiene_actions returned a 'Update pricing to rounded off pricing' item affecting 454 SKUs at 1-2 rupee adjustments each (e.g. Weave-Studio-febrizo-WARLI-TEXTURE-CHIKKU Rs.800 -> Rs.799.0, VICENZALIFESTYLE-Royal-Hiran-RED Rs.6400 -> Rs.6399.0). Most deltas are ±1 to ±3 rupees. These affect how the storefront prices display — best done before ads point at listings — but are not a launch blocker in the same way online pay is. SKU count: 454 (per fetch_hygiene_actions.details). North star orders, expected impact 2026-11-07 — in line with the strategy; action should clear before the campaign's first paid impressions. Note: this changes the listed price of YEru2vIx1WG0 (Warli-CHIKKU) from Rs.800 to Rs.799, which is why the strategy's launch-set item 1 dropped that SKU from the campaign., Post-launch hygiene (week 2): size charts on Angel x lady kurti/co-ord line + tag uncategorised SKU. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Address the 13 size-chart gaps on the 'Angel x lady' kurti/co-ord family SKUs (D.NO-0002-B-orange, D.NO.-069 aqua blue, D.NO.-032 Mendhi, D.NO.-069 Orange, D.NO.-010 -Mendhi, R- 023 PInk, R-003, D.NO.-010 -Brown, D.NO.-044 White, R- 023 Sky Blue, D.NO.-0001 --White, D.NO-0003, C-05) and tag the uncategorised SKU 'Angel x lady D.NO-0002-A' (per fetch_hygiene_actions). Schedule for week 2, NOT before launch — these SKUs are not on the launch set and cannot affect launch performance.

Reasoning:
Per fetch_hygiene_actions: 13 SKUs in the 'Angel x lady' family lack size charts, and 'Angel x lady D.NO-0002-A' is uncategorised. None of these SKUs are on the launch product set (the launch set spans Weave-Studio-febrizo and Maruti-18_19). Treating them as launch-blockers is wrong — they cannot affect launch performance. Addressing them is right for the account but wrong for this run's bandwidth. Schedule for week 2; address only if launch read surfaces them as load-bearing. Action type is unset (no automation route): catalogue / size-chart work is hand-done. North star orders, expected impact deferred to a later week; this action is hygiene that follows the launch, not a launch input.

Start a new open audience video campaign with age 18-35 at Rs.1,000/day, running on the hoodie hero (Rs.999), the oversized tee (Rs.549 after the price move), and the polo (Rs.599 after the price move). India-wide, no exclusions. ROAS floor 5.34. The product set is menswear end-to-end, so the audience self-filters on gender through the landing page.

Reasoning:
Pre-live account with no pixel history. Open Audience is the right first-campaign type because Lookalike needs a seed the account does not have and Advantage+ needs pixel data the account does not have. Campaign routing recommendation returned no row for this seller (NOT CHECKED), so the choice rests on the absence of pixel history. Category benchmark S/GMV is 13.1% on mens-clothing (100/13.1 ≈ 7.63 GMV/rupee); 70% of that = 5.34, set as the ROAS floor so the campaign can find a bid on day one — a first campaign on day one has no learning behind it, so the floor is conservative; the ceiling is the category figure. Product set is the three COGS-clean men's apparel SKUs after the price moves above: hoodie at Rs.999 (AOV anchor, 35.0% COGS, no change), oversized tee at Rs.549 (42.8% COGS), polo at Rs.599 (39.2% COGS). One campaign = one ad set = one creative; the launch budget is not split across cold starts. Age 18-35, India-wide, ROAS floor 5.34. The video render is in flight (handle job_DgGr1bMREywV); the campaign is held until the asset is ready. The action stage started the render in the same turn; a placeholder would be refused. The strategy's spec also named gender=men; the campaign spec accepts only one narrowing (age OR gender), so gender was dropped. The product set is menswear end-to-end, so the audience self-filters on gender through the landing page. Item 3 of the work order., Mirror the Rs.449 → Rs.549 hike on the duplicate oversized-tee SKUs. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Ask seller to mirror the Rs.449 → Rs.549 hike on the duplicate oversized-tee SKUs under the same physical product as amazon_B0HKMS263L. Affected seller_sku_ids: 9suAlBzRuZXp (amazon_B0G8J67ZK6), DlpPS2G7DIKz (amazon_B0F89B4CZD), vWaVpghhvfCc (amazon_B0HKMPQNGX), 4TnvP4Yrjc0I (amazon_B0HJWSTBR8), cGhbVUjB3rU1 (amazon_B0HKMRXWGK), UpZ7vnsKMV4d (amazon_B0HJWH9G8K), 72XuUaNUi8EB (amazon_B0F89DG52V), 3FpgsjxRQYeI (amazon_B0HJWJDWRZ). The single update on RP2XEjjoYGHM does not propagate; without mirroring, the campaign will route spend to whichever SKU the catalogue surfaces at the lower Rs.449 and the margin move does not hold.

Reasoning:
Eight duplicate seller_sku_ids (excluding RP2XEjjoYGHM itself) carry the same 240 GSM cotton oversized tee at Rs.449 in the catalogue read of 2026-10-17. The price update on RP2XEjjoYGHM is per-product; it does not propagate. The COGS-over-50% hygiene flag covers several of these duplicates. Without mirroring, the campaign's effective AOV on the tee line falls back to Rs.449, and the new margin does not hold. Seller-side change; no automation route. Item 4 of the work order., Confirm the hoodie video creative within 5 business days. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Ask seller to confirm a video creative for the hoodie hero shot within 5 business days so the action stage can start (or replace) the render. Brief: 15s single_video, Premium Ad angle, on-screen copy "320 GSM Cotton Pullover Hoodie — Kangaroo Pocket, Relaxed Fit, Rs.999", product = amazon_B0HMD1RLRT (Mens Premium Pullover Hoodie, Oat Milk). The action stage has already started one render (handle job_DgGr1bMREywV) — the seller's role is to supply replacement footage or product shots if the first render needs it. If no video can be had at all, the action stage falls back to a single-image catalogue campaign on the same product set.

Seller-side change. The launch brief is video (single_video) on the hoodie; a render is a scheduling fact and not a format input. The action stage started the render in the same turn (handle job_DgGr1bMREywV); the seller ask is to surface the deadline and to supply replacement footage if the first render needs it. Without a video the format fallback is catalogue, not video-on-banner. Item 5 of the work order., Switch Push for online payments to ON in storefront settings. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Ask seller to switch Push for online payments ON in the storefront settings. Current value: push_for_online_payments = false. Category benchmark cancellation is 18.6% on mens-clothing and the seller is COD-heavy by default; a small push toward prepaid softens both RTO and customer-cancellation risk.

Reasoning:
Seller-side change. push_for_online_payments does not move the campaign outcome directly, but a COD-led buyer's RTO risk is structurally higher; flipping the flag to ON nudges the checkout toward prepaid without removing COD. Seller-consent, not an operator flip. Verified current value false in get_seller_website_checkout_config on 2026-10-17. Update selling price for amazon_B0HKMS263L (Mens 240 Gsm Cotton Oversized Tee) to Rs.549.

Verified against the catalogue read of 2026-10-17; all 5 SKUs under the product are at Rs.499 today. Item 2 of the work order.

There is no automation route for "operator-confirmed precondition check" — emit as no-action_type with the verification steps in instruction_text., Build and activate launch campaign — Bhram Launch — Open Audience — Video 5SKUs. |DETAILS|  Instruction:

One-campaign launch rule binds; no parallel campaign is created. product_set_ids is not sent — single_video is not catalog, so it is ignored. creative_asset = job_N3HykPja4e6u (render handle from item 9)., Add 'online' to settings_payment_mode. |DETAILS|  Instruction:

Online payment is the lever that closes the structural RTO problem on this L2. Enable online payment before launch. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Ask the seller (Fox Number Plates) to enable at least one payment gateway (Razorpay, Paytm or Easebuzz) on their storefront and add 'online' to settings_payment_mode before the launch campaign goes live. Current state on 2026-10-15: settings_payment_mode = 'cod' only, all three gateways off. Target: at least one gateway flag true AND 'online' present in settings_payment_mode. Decision rule: if no gateway is live by 2026-10-22, hold the launch campaign and re-scope.

Reasoning:
HIGH hygiene item from fetch_hygiene_actions for account_stage=hit, seller_consent=false (so this is a seller-comms task, not a Shopdeck-side change). Verified current state on 2026-10-15 via get_seller_website_checkout_config: settings_payment_mode='cod', is_paytm=false, is_razorpay=false, is_easebuzz=false, push_for_online_payments=false. Category benchmark bm_rto=40.97% from get_seller_category_level_benchmarking means a 100% COD campaign sees ~4 in 10 orders RTO. At the ₹1,500/day launch budget and category-typical C2PR, that is ~10–12 RTO orders per day — survivable for one week of learning, not steady state. Online pay needs both a gateway flag and 'online' in the payment mode list; the seller controls both. This is the launch blocker — the Open Audience campaign (₹1,500/day, 12-product catalogue set, ROAS floor 4.5) and the price cuts (₹1,599→₹1,149 etc.) the campaign's floor math rests on both ship after this is verified.

Launch Open Audience campaign on 6 hero-flavour jowar puff SKUs at Rs.1000/day. |DETAILS|  Instruction:

Reasoning:
Pre-live Hits account, 0 weeks of marketing spend, no customer file, no pixel history. Open Audience is the launch-progression first stage when neither a lookalike seed (no orders) nor a pixel with purchase events (no traffic) exists. The 6 single-flavour hero SKUs (vs 26 multi-flavour multipacks) let Meta learn one flavour × audience pairing at a time, instead of splitting the cold-start budget across 32 cold products. The launch budget of Rs.1,000/day is the cold-start size per the pre-live progression rule — the seller's aspirational required_spend of Rs.10,000/day is the scale target after week-one delivery confirms a working audience-product pair. Sources: get_seller_account_age (0 weeks of spend), get_seller_config_build (account_stage=hit, ad_account_id=1469498545022821, required_spend=10000), get_seller_catalogue (32 products), get_seller_category_level_benchmarking (bm_s_gmv 36.9%). A flat Rs 50 off, or a percentage of AOV (recommended 5%), both work — the seller chooses, but the value must be > 0. This is a seller-consent flip; the seller is the actor (hygiene pull reports seller_consent=false). Hygiene finding: MEDIUM 'Online discount has been set to zero, please add a non-zero value'. Without this, a buyer choosing online has no rupee incentive to do so over COD; on the wider seller population, raising online_max_discount to a non-zero value is one of the most reliable levers on prepaid share and (downstream) RTO. Warning: a non-zero online discount set too high (> Rs 200 flat) cannibalizes contribution margin on the prepaid orders it generates — the right number is the smallest value that moves the order mix, the seller decides.

Reasoning:
Strategy spec 4, sub-task (2). On its own this is the second hygiene finding (MEDIUM 'Online discount has been set to zero'). Compound finding 1 (no online mode) with this and the buyer has zero reason to pick prepaid over COD even if a gateway were integrated. Without a rupee incentive the order mix does not shift and the RTO benefit does not land., Turn on push_for_online_payments on the storefront (seller comm). |DETAILS|  Instruction:

Without the nudge, even with online payment enabled and a non-zero online discount, COD buyers do not switch by default — the upfront pricing advantage has to be the option the checkout is steering them toward. Hygiene finding adjacent: HIGH 'Enable Online Payment' (the underlying hygiene row covers both that the mode is missing and that the nudge is off — both belong to the same checkout-side fix).

Reasoning:
Strategy spec 4, sub-task (3). The other two hygiene flips (online mode + non-zero discount) shift the structural option set; the nudge is what tips the marginal buyer. The prepaid-share and RTO benefit of the first two flips will not show up at scale without the checkout actively steering buyers.

Open seller-comms ticket: "Lust Breaker" adult-products catalogue is blocked by Meta policy; ask seller to pick a path before any campaign is built. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
Open one seller-comms ticket on seller 6ab4d563f152a249271776f4 ("Lust Breaker"). The ticket must (a) state plainly that the current 16-SKU catalogue is blocked from Meta advertising under Meta's Health and Wellness policy because every product is a sexual-pleasure / adult-intimacy item (vibrators, butt plugs, penis sleeves, realistic dildos, panty vibrators, handheld masturbators, massagers), and that the sexual-wellness exception covers only health-framed products (contraceptives, menopause, ED, premature ejaculation, pelvic-floor care, sex education); (b) name the three durable paths the seller can take — (1) stay on Meta and add health-framed sexual-wellness SKUs to the existing brand, advertising only those; (2) stay on the current catalogue and move paid traffic off Meta to Google Search / YouTube / direct-affiliate networks; (3) fully reposition the brand in a medical / wellness register; and (c) ask the seller to confirm the chosen path in writing before any campaign, budget, audience, creative or pricing work begins. Do not build a campaign, do not pick a product set, do not pick a budget, do not pick audiences or creatives, until the seller has chosen. After the seller responds, re-run the troubleshoot so the next run can diagnose the chosen path.

Reasoning:
The diagnosis (sections 2 and 5) established that all 16 SKUs are in scope of Meta's Health and Wellness adult-products ban (pleasure-focused items; the sexual-wellness exception is health-framed only) and that no campaign type, bid strategy, budget, audience, creative or pricing change moves past this catalogue-level restriction. The policy is global and applies in India. Internal pricing similarity returns zero matches for any of the 16 SKUs (no Shopdeck seller in the match index competes on these products), so "price changes based on internal similar products" is unanswerable from the data even setting the policy block aside, and web search is moot while ads cannot run. The strategy stage therefore refuses to open a campaign bet on Meta and instead opens a seller-comms bet to force the path choice; the north star is "first Meta-delivered order on a non-blocked SKU within 60 days of the seller picking a path," and the only thing that moves it is the seller adding path-1 SKUs, picking path 2, or doing path 3. This action is the lever because without the path choice there is nothing the action stage can do on Meta. Expected impact: a written seller path-selection response within 14 days of the comms ticket (early read); the first Meta-delivered order on a non-blocked SKU within 60 days of that selection (north star). Side-effect tripwire: with COD-only and no payment gateway integrated, expect RTO on the first non-blocked SKUs to run above category norm; if RTO exceeds category benchmark by more than 10 percentage points within 30 days of first delivered orders, pause spend and re-diagnose before adding budget.

Reasoning:
The diagnose stage pulled the checkout config: payment_charges_online_max_discount is 0 and discount_type is 'fixed'. Without a non-zero online discount, every order defaults to partial-COD, which carries higher RTO risk than prepaid — and a pre-live launch with no RTO history cannot afford that. Razorpay is already enabled, and 'online' is the first entry in settings_payment_mode, so the prepaid path is live; only the discount lever is missing. Picking a flat Rs. 50 (the strategy's recommendation) because (a) the existing discount_type is already 'fixed', so only the cap changes; (b) the catalogue AOV band is ₹599–₹1,059, so Rs. 50 is ~5–8% of order, in the band where prepaid nudges work; (c) Rs. 50 preserves more margin than a percentage discount on the higher-AOV SKUs. This is one of three preconditions the launch campaign depends on; the other two (Meta ad account id; creative production) are out of Shopdeck automation and are flagged in the narrative.

The change is multi-step: (1) work with the seller to choose ONE of Paytm or Razorpay and complete the provider's KYC / integration; (2) flip the chosen gateway flag on the storefront; (3) add "online" to settings_payment_mode. The settings_payment_mode change is a single field edit; the gateway integration is an external step (KYC + account creation) that takes days, so the action is sent as a manual task with no action_type set., Tag 3 untagged products (6aOvNAv8IB8y, 7hIKHlBLlKR5, jW94p34n9JIV) with the right L1-L4 category slugs. |DETAILS|  Instruction:
